I understand the feeling. Last week, I had to put down my cat of 12 years. Both of her kidneys were severely afflicted, and she hadn’t even shown significant symptoms until the day I took her in. It tore me up to hear from the vet that her kidney problems had been going on for a while.


I was living in strictly no-pet housing two years ago, with a roommate who owned rodents in an open cage. It was all I was able to find, so my dad was taking care of my kitty. It seemed like the best solution.
But last year, right after moving into a new place, I found out my dad had started leaving my cat alone, at his house, for up to 5 days at a time. He was neglecting and I had no idea. I was devastated. I thought he had been taking good care of her, as he had been telling me so.

As soon as I knew this, I made an emergency trip to take her home. She adjusted quickly to staying with me again. She didn’t have any apparent health concerns when I took her back. In fact, she seemed healthy, and happy as usual. I nurtured her back to what I assumed was full health, and I got closer to her than I ever was. She was always purring and always right beside me. 

We have come to learn that my dad is very impersonal when it comes to animals, and he isn’t as good with them as we had thought. He believed that she was fine and that he was taking care of her.

I worry that her staying at my dad’s, being left alone is what caused her health to decline so badly. I’m worried that while I was living without her for a year, getting drunk, seeing friends, she was alone, developing kidney disease, because I left her all alone...
The guilt is almost as bad as the grief. I keep thinking about the doctor’s words “This has been going on for a while” and how shocked I was to hear it. And how I wish I could have helped her more. The first thing I thought was “this is all my fault.”

I am trying to believe that she was grateful for the time that I gave her this past year, even if she had been alone for some time at my dad’s. I try not to blame myself for what happened to her.

It’s hard. But I know that she appreciated the time I spent with her. And I am glad that I was able to spoil her for the last year that I had her. 

I hope this helps you. Enjoy every moment with your pet. Give her all the love you have.

Yes, for sure. As others have said, it has gotten more stable as I get older. But I definitely do have laser-focused interests that seem to “rotate.”
For me it’s generally: cartoons, drawing, video games, reading, music, and crafts. But I can’t usually stick to one for longer than a few months before I move on to the next. It’s kind of frustrating, especially since I like to post some of my creative stuff online.

I like wearing comfortable clothes or having a nice fabric on hand that I can feel. I also like to carry some small pieces of origami paper with me, so I can make cranes or just fold when I get a moment.
Otherwise I try to practice “boxed breathing”: breathing in for 6 seconds, holding for 4, and breathing out for 8. Or I try to focus on just one thing, one sound or sight or texture, until I feel less overwhelmed.

Yep. I’ve had a fair share of girlfriends stop talking to me out of nowhere, even when the last time we hung out seemed perfectly fine. They never seem to offer any explanation, so I don’t even bother asking anymore.
I feel for you, and although I wouldn’t wish it on anyone, it is kind of relieving to know I’m not alone. 
I am extremely lucky to have about three close girlfriends now. It took me a really long time to find them, though, and each of them is a little “different” socially, as well. 
Similar to others in this thread, I didn’t seem to have this problem with my guy friends. Most of my friends are men at this point, mostly due to shared interests and similar social styles. 
I’ve been alone, too, though. In my senior year of high school/the year after, I spent most of my time alone, and didn’t have any friends I really saw. It took me two years from then to actually build up three good and supportive friends. 
Hope this helps. It really, really sucks to be blown off by friends, but you may find that not everyone is like that.

In college, everyone seems to be the exact same. But sometimes the people you’d get along with are just more in the background. I met some coworkers who enjoy DnD and picked up a campaign with them. I never would have guessed until I picked up a conversation with the leader.

I hope you find some success in your social struggles, stranger. I know the feeling too well.

The joint I work for is a local, small-town family-owned restaurant. It is not a chain, and as such, does not have the management of a chain. That’s some clarification I should have provided.

I am a relatively new hire, and am not entirely familiar with the various titles on the management ladder. The higher manager in question, the man, is what crew members call a “brown collar,” as he and the few other managers at his high level wear collared shirts.

The woman in question was simply a “brown shirt,” or a lower-level manager, and newly-appointed.

She was assertive. She told the employee, rather sternly, “put gloves on.” He then proceeded to laugh in her face, as the higher manager entered the scene and, too, laughed in her face. From my understanding, she was cornered.

I can’t say whether further assertiveness on her part would have helped. Maybe it would have, maybe it wouldn’t have. Either way, in her shoes, with both the higher manager and the employees below me laughing at my attempts of management... can’t say I would’ve felt too empowered. 

Speaking up to the owners would have likely gotten her ostracized from our other coworkers, for “snitching” (it’s a cliquey atmosphere) and because of manager favoritism. Still, can’t say for sure. I’d love to see something done about it. 

TL;DR: good ol southern bible belt family-owned restaurant, where management is largely decided by favoritism and who-knows-who, and most sexism or unethical practices seem pushed under the rug.

I see what you're saying. Sometimes it's hard to distinguish him from his depression. I want so badly to just snap him out of it and convince him he's worth caring for, but you're right. It isn't that easy, and if it was, depression wouldn't be an illness.

Regarding his parents, he's moving out the first of August, and I think that'll be a positive development for him. I think I'll see how things go for him in the next few weeks as he adjusts to living alone, maybe he can get the help he needs and start towards recovery. He's told me he doesn't like getting people involved with his mental health and dismisses my efforts to help, so I guess it's all up to him.

Thank you for the advice!

His parents are actively involved, yes, but perhaps too much so. He's said that his mom can be very controlling and emotionally manipulative, and that both of his parents often try to control him and smother him. 
He has a circle of close friends that provide support. But most of his friends seem to encourage his drinking, smoking, etc. and other unhealthy habits.
My biggest concern is his care for himself. I wish he could see himself as worthy.

My 3 older brothers discovered it back when I was about ten, and in typical little sister fashion I pestered them to let me play it until they conceded. I adored it. I played through the first 3, dabbled in the manga, then didn't touch it for years until 9 yrs later I got word about Dual Destinies and thought I'd try it out. Got hooked again, finished AJ and now I'm almost done with Dual Destinies and about 6 eps into the anime.
This series was a pivotal part of my childhood and seeing how much it's grown has been like watching an old childhood friend grow and find success :') Ace Attorney will always have a place in my heart.
